 "score_claims": "README states real practice scores of 3.71 / 4.44 / 4.75 for three successive versions (their own simulator gave 4.1 / 4.9 / 5.5 for the same versions) and 1.15 real for the kit example (sim ~1.2). The current head (called v0.5, quiet movement on by default) is given as 4.54 real in the comparison with the hide-and-wait probe, which scored 4.04 real (probe commit 42d652b). All other numbers in the repo are from their own simulators, not the real scorer.",
 "architecture": "One Python file, one decision function per observation, no learning. It is a fixed-priority rule ladder, not a utility system; only target choice and cover choice use scores. Aim/fire is decided first and independently of movement, so the bot keeps shooting whatever movement mode it is in. Per tick: (1) read events (damage log over 2.5 s gives incoming DPS; attacker ids with timestamps; kill time), remember threat sounds; (2) pick upgrade if offered; (3) zone state; (4) refresh crate/pickup memory; (5) build enemy list with map line of sight from eye and from muzzle; add a pseudo-threat 120 m along the damage bearing for any attacker not currently known (last 1.5 s); (6) pickup wanted/take; (7) target choice; (8) crate/NPC farm target if no shootable mech; (9) aim and fire; (10) dodge vector; (11) movement mode; (12) A* waypoint, 16-direction local steering, dodge blend, quiet-speed cap, stuck/climb logic. Movement mode order, first match wins: zone-urgent (outside or within 8 m of the edge) > cover (if retreating, or 'many', or outranged, and not in a close fight/finish) > zone must-go > [hold, only with the patient switch] > cube > arm-up loot > fight > loot > roam. Definitions: retreating is a latch set when HP < 38% with a threat visible and released at HP > 80% or (12 s without damage and HP > 60%); 'many' = 3+ visible threats within 240 m, or 2+ with own HP < 60%, or incoming DPS > 110/s, or any unseen attacker; outranged = a visible laser holder beyond 70 m while we have no laser; close fight = shootable target under 40 m and (we hold lightning or HP > 50%); finishing = shootable target at or below 30% HP within 130 m, own HP > 30%, at most 2 real threats. Strategy switches are read from an environment variable so several variants can be A/B tested from one file. Time guard: far-enemy sight checks are skipped after 15 ms, A* only steps before ~20-26 ms, cover search stops at 28-33 ms.",
 "navigation": "Map model: every building prism is scan-line rasterised into a 2 m grid storing one lowest base and one highest top per cell, plus the 1 m terrain grid. Line of sight is a sampled march along the segment (2.5 m steps, 4 m for cover checks) testing whether the sample height lies between base and top of its cell or under terrain; trees are not modelled at all. A point is 'blocked' for walking if it is within 4 m of the map edge, if a prism rises more than 1.3 m above the feet and starts below head height (so high bridges can be walked under), or if terrain rises more than about 1.4 m plus 0.55 m per metre of probe distance (a crude slope limit). Nav grid: 4 m cells, a cell is free when its centre and four points 2.5 m around it are unblocked (mech radius baked in, fixed, not grown with cubes). A* is 8-connected with no corner cutting, octile heuristic, uniform cost (no threat or exposure cost), capped at 25,000 expansions, and incremental: it works in slices across ticks until a per-tick deadline. Before planning it tests whether the straight line to the goal is free (then no path is needed); a path or running search is reused while the goal stays within 4 cells of the planned goal; failed searches impose a 2 s cool-down. Path following takes the nearest path point in a small window and steers to the farthest waypoint within 32 m of path length that has a clear straight line; more than 28 m off route forces a replan. Pathing is skipped in fight mode and whenever the mech is more than 3 m above terrain (roof or airborne). Local steering picks the best of 16 headings: alignment with the desired direction plus a small bonus for keeping the previous heading, minus penalties if blocked at 3, 6 or 10 m. Stuck handling has two layers: a speed check (commanding movement but under 2.5 m/s on the ground for ~0.6 s) which starts a 2.5 s 'climb' (jump, then jet while airborne, steering straight at the goal) if the obstacle 4 m ahead is less than 40 m tall and energy > 35, otherwise a random sideways detour for 1.5 s; and a progress watchdog every 2.5 s (goal more than 20 m away, moved less than 5 m, not under fire) which forces a replan and on the second consecutive trip jets over the obstacle. Roofs are used only incidentally: short jet hops to reach a wanted pickup lying more than 1.5 m above when within 14 m, and the stuck climb. Boost is used for zone urgency, for distant loot/cubes when no real threat is within 80 m (hysteresis: start above 60 energy, stop near 22), and for dodges and fleeing just after being hit.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Aim point is the body centre (half height, scaled by the target's cube count). Gun lead: two fixed-point iterations of time of flight = distance / bullet speed plus 0.05 s latency, linear target velocity, vertical lead clamped to +/-6 m. Gun fires only when yaw error is inside an angular window of about 1.6 target radii at that distance (plus ~0.7 deg) and pitch error inside about 3 m at that distance, the target is inside gun range minus 3 m, and the magazine is loaded. There is no hit-probability or range gating beyond that: it shoots out to ~227 m. Laser: starts charging as soon as any shootable mech or drone is within laser range minus 5 m and the cooldown is over (crates only if it has no gun); holds the trigger until full charge (0.75 s), then releases on the first tick the beam solution (target position led by only 0.1 s) is inside the same angular window; while fully charged the torso aims with the laser solution instead of the gun lead; if the hold is about to hit the forced auto-fire time and aim is off, it releases anyway. With no target it keeps holding a started charge (up to ~1.5 s past full) while any enemy is still remembered. Lightning: fired whenever the target is inside its range minus 1 m, energy covers the cost plus 1, and the target bearing is within 40% of the cone angle of the current torso yaw. All held weapons fire together. Reload policy: reload early only when there is nothing to shoot and the magazine is under 60%; otherwise run dry. With no target the torso looks, in order, at an unseen attacker's damage bearing, the last damage bearing (3 s), the nearest remembered enemy, the last threat sound (2 s), else it spins continuously at about 3.5 rad/s to scan. If hit by an attacker it cannot see and the current target is not within 45 m, it stops shooting (unless a laser charge is in progress) and turns to face the hit direction, which also protects the rear arc. Target choice score (lowest wins): distance + 0.2 x target HP, minus 100 if at or below 30% HP, minus 120 for the current target (stickiness), minus 40 if it damaged us in the last 4 s, plus 400 if not shootable, plus 1000 beyond 285 m.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Nothing is specific to the squad schedule (no notion of one early hunter, escalation or the late all-in); the survival layer is generic. Cover mode (triggers above) searches 16 directions x 7 radii (7, 14, 22, 32, 44, 58, 75 m), only along rays that are walkable in a straight line from the current position; each candidate is scored 100 per threat eye (three nearest threats, including the 120 m pseudo-threat for an unseen shooter) that has sight of the candidate at 90% eye height, plus 0.8 per metre of distance, minus a small bonus for heading away from the mean threat bearing, plus heavy penalties for points outside the current or (when it must move) next circle. A zero-sightline cover point is kept for up to 4 s and re-verified every third tick; otherwise recomputed every 4 ticks. It boosts toward cover if hit in the last 2 s with energy > 30. Fallbacks when no hidden point exists and a target is shootable: if gun-only and a laser/lightning pickup is within 90 m and HP > 30%, go arm up; otherwise stand and trade; if outranged by a laser with HP > 50% and at most one real threat, charge the sniper to 22 m with boost. Fight movement: hold a preferred range (110 m with laser, 28 m with lightning only or when holding both and the target is under 60 m, 85 m gun-only, 28/55 m when finishing) using a radial term proportional to range error over 30 m plus 0.85 lateral strafe; strafe side flips with 70% probability every 1.0-2.6 s. Dodging: sidestep out of the aim line of any visible charging laser (corridor 7 m plus 3% of distance, sticky side per enemy, boost if energy > 30) unless holding lightning within 40 m, in which case it stays and zaps to short the laser; sidestep bullets whose closest approach is within 3.8 m in the next 0.45 s; forward-simulate mortar shells and run directly out of a 13 m landing radius, boosting if impact is under 1.2 s away. Regeneration is implicit only: it relies on reaching a point with no sightlines; there is no explicit hold-fire/regen timer state, and the retreat latch only releases at 80% HP. Quiet movement (default on): when enemies are known or a threat sound was heard within 8 s, nobody has hit it for 3 s, and it is roaming, collecting a cube, holding or in cover, speed is capped at 4.6 m/s so it emits no step sound (protocol threshold 5 m/s). Optional 'patient' switch (off by default): only open fire when cheap (target under 55 m, under 55% HP, attacked us within 6 s, charging a laser, facing more than 75 deg away from us, or 4 or fewer alive), otherwise hide and hold position for 2 s after breaking sight.",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "Wanted weapons are laser and lightning only; mortar is never picked up (laser cook-off risk and the laser bonus against mortar holders) and is dropped first if somehow held. The first wanted pickup goes into the empty slot; the second replaces the GUN, so the end loadout is laser + lightning with no gun. Search radius for a wanted pickup is 240 m while holding neither special weapon and 160 m otherwise, height difference at most 25 m, and it must lie inside the 'safe' circle unless within 30 m. Arm-up-first rule: while gun-only, not hit in the last 1.5 s, and the target is absent, beyond 50 m, or the pickup is within 20 m, looting outranks fighting. Pickups and crates seen earlier are remembered and forgotten only when the bot is within 28 m with sight of the spot and the item is absent (or a take succeeds/fails). Cubes: a visible cube within 70 m at about the same height inside the safe circle outranks fighting when HP > 35%, at most one real threat is visible, and the cube is within 10 m or the target is unshootable or beyond 60 m; this is how kill drops are collected immediately. Farming when no mech is shootable: nearest of crates within 150 m or drones within 140 m (drones penalised by 30 m and only at HP > 55%) with muzzle line of sight; it approaches to 22 m of a crate and 50 m of a drone (outside the 45 m aggro radius) and shoots. Supply drops: only when no threats and HP > 45%, within 170 m, if it lands no later than arrival time plus 8 s, skipped when another mech has already banked more than 1.5 s of capture. Roam order: cube (within 120 m) > supply drop > farm target > remembered crate within 260 m (HP > 60%, no threats) > drift toward the next circle centre until inside 55% of its radius > stand still. Upgrade priority, best first: plating, armor, nanites (all survivability), then laser damage, lightning efficiency, gun rate, laser charge, gun damage, capacitor, reactor, gyros, lightning range, gun magazine, sensors, gun velocity, servos, jets, lightning chain, laser pierce, and mortar upgrades last.",
 "zone_and_endgame": "The current circle is interpolated linearly during a shrink. Margin = min(30 m, 30% of next radius); 'need' = distance to the next centre minus (next radius minus margin). Must-go when need / walk speed + 12 s exceeds the time to shrink start (or shrink end once shrinking); an optional 'early' switch uses 24 s and tested slightly negative. Urgent = outside the zone or within 8 m of the current edge; urgent zone travel overrides everything including cover, while non-urgent must-go ranks below cover. Zone goal is the next centre, with a detour to a wanted pickup within 25 m; boost when urgent (energy > 25) or when more than 60 m of ground must be made up (energy > 60). Any other mode's goal outside the next circle is replaced by the next centre while must-go; cover candidates outside the circle are heavily penalised; loot, cubes, crates and drops are only pursued inside the 'safe' area (next circle minus half the margin, or 25 m inside the current circle when not pressed). Distances are straight-line, not path lengths. There is no endgame logic at all: no special handling of the 25 m and 0 m circles, no late-match stance, no awareness of how many opponents remain except inside the off-by-default patient switch.",
 "housebot_observations": "Two real-scorer observations are documented. (1) The practice score is deterministic: resubmitting identical code returned the identical score. (2) Real house bots hunt a passive bot less aggressively than the authors' model: the hide-and-wait probe scored 4.04 real against a simulator prediction of about 3.2-3.3, while the normal bot scored 4.54 real against 5.40 in the simulator. Everything else about house bots is the authors' ASSUMPTION encoded in their stand-in simulator, not an observation: all 15 hunt our bot from the start if it is inside a tier-specific chase radius (easy 150 m, medium 260 m, hard 420 m, expert unlimited), otherwise they drift to the next circle; they approach to 90 m then circle-strafe, never boost or jump; firing ranges 110/140/170/200 m by tier; Gaussian aim noise of 4.0/2.5/1.3/0.7 degrees by tier multiplied by 5; the three strongest carry lasers; shared targeting, no friendly fire. That model was tuned so the kit example scores ~1.2 (real 1.15) and it overestimates their own bot by about 0.4-0.75 points (4.1/4.9/5.5 simulated vs 3.71/4.44/4.75 real). The repo has tools to profile first-minute deaths by attacker tier and arming time, but no recorded outputs.",

  "Real practice scores by version: 3.71, 4.44, 4.75; kit example 1.15. Their practice simulator read 4.1, 4.9, 5.5 and ~1.2 for the same bots, i.e. it overestimates a competent bot by 0.4-0.75.",
  "Real scoring is deterministic: identical code resubmitted gave the identical score (so a submission can be used as a clean A/B probe).",
  "Hide-and-wait ('patient': hold fire at range, break sight, sit still) scored 4.04 real versus 4.54 real for the normal bot (-0.50), although their simulator predicted 3.19 versus 5.40; in their 16-bot free-for-all league the same switch was +0.36 +/- 0.22 over 168 matches. Passivity costs in practice mode but helps in a free-for-all.",
  "Quiet movement (speed capped at 4.6 m/s when enemies are known/heard and not under fire): practice sim 5.25 vs 5.40 (neutral, slightly negative), league +0.2 to +0.65; they left it on. No real-scorer number for it in this repo.",
  "Faster strafe direction flips ('jink', every 0.35-0.9 s instead of 1.0-2.6 s): league +0.17, within noise; left off.",
  "Arriving in the next circle earlier (24 s buffer instead of 12 s): league -0.14, within noise; left off.",
  "Tighter laser release tolerance: league -0.25 (noise), measured accuracy unchanged; left off.",
  "A* navigation versus the previous steering-only version: practice sim +0.4 (noise), league -0.14 +/- 0.26; kept only because it fixes a real stuck-in-a-pocket bug.",
  "Oracle upper bounds in their league (capability granted to 4 of 16 mechs, paired, 120 matches each): damage taken -30% gives +1.65 (se 0.29); max HP +30% gives +1.36 (se 0.28); 360-degree vision to 300 m plus 1.5x hearing gives +0.90 (se 0.29); damage dealt +30% gives +0.63 (se 0.34); hit boxes 1.5x wider (gun hit rate about 44% to 65%) gives only +0.28 (se 0.27).",
  "Cube economy in the league with crates, drones, drops and upgrades modelled: starting with 5 cubes is worth +1.02, with 10 cubes +1.67 (se 0.29); their normal bot ends a match with about 6 cubes on average.",
  "Their stated conclusion: survivability dominates, aiming improvements are worth almost nothing, and the cube economy is the only large legitimate source of effective HP.",
  "Caveat on all of the above except the real scores: oracle and switch numbers come from their own simplified free-for-all simulator (no mortar, approximate hit boxes and vision), not from the real practice mode against a coordinated squad; most A/B deltas are inside one or two standard errors."

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Oracle ablations: grant a capability for free (less damage taken, more HP, better vision, more damage, wider hit boxes) to rank where engineering effort can pay before building anything.",
  "Use the deterministic real scorer as a measurement instrument: submit a deliberately different probe build and compare with the baseline, then recalibrate the local simulator from the gap.",
  "Env-variable strategy switches plus a paired league where several variants of the same bot play in the same matches with slot shuffling, reporting paired difference and standard error.",
  "Silent walking: stay under the 5 m/s step-sound threshold when enemies are near but not shooting, to deny sound-based tracking.",
  "Pseudo-threat for an unseen attacker: place a virtual enemy 120 m along the damage bearing so cover search and the 'outnumbered' test react to shooters that are not visible, and turn the torso toward it to protect the rear arc.",
  "Lightning as an anti-laser tool: when a charging laser holder is within 40 m and lightning is available, stay and zap (shorts the laser) instead of dodging.",
  "Laser-line dodge with a sticky side per enemy so the bot does not oscillate across the beam; mortar landing-point prediction against roof/terrain height and running out of the splash radius; bullet closest-approach sidestep.",
  "Arm up before fighting: gun-only bots prioritise a laser/lightning pickup up to 240 m away; when caught in the open with no cover and only a gun, either go arm up or rush a laser sniper to 22 m rather than trade at range.",
  "Cover search scored by counting threat eyes with sight of each candidate point, with a kept-while-valid cache re-verified every third tick.",
  "Incremental A* spread over several ticks under a wall-clock deadline, with a straight-line-free shortcut test and goal-drift tolerance to avoid replanning.",
  "Two-layer stuck handling: speed-based check plus a slower net-progress watchdog that escalates from replan to jetting over the obstacle.",
  "Memory of crates and pickups with invalidation only when the spot is seen empty from close range.",
  "Free-for-all engagement etiquette (for the final): start a fight only when it is cheap (close, weakened target, target's back turned by more than 75 degrees, it attacked first, or few mechs left).",
  "Drone farming from 50 m (outside the 45 m aggro radius) and crate farming from 22 m; supply-drop arrival-time check and skipping drops another mech is already capturing."

  "Regeneration is not managed: there is no hold-fire state or regen timer. Firing is decided independently of movement, so while retreating it keeps shooting any shootable mech, and once hidden it will shoot visible crates (and drones above 55% HP), which keeps resetting the 5 s no-damage-dealt timer. The retreat latch needs 80% HP to release.",
  "Laser charging starts whenever a target is shootable, including while fleeing to cover, and charging halves movement speed; retreat is therefore often at half speed.",
  "It drops the gun for the second special weapon, leaving laser + lightning: beyond 45 m the only damage is one beam per ~2.4 s, and lightning draws from the same energy pool as boost and jets.",
  "Gun fires at any range out to ~227 m with only an angular gate and no hit-probability or exposure consideration: wastes magazines, makes noise, resets regen.",
  "Line of sight ignores trees (trunks and canopy) completely and is a coarse sampled march over a 2 m raster with one base/top pair per cell (4 m samples in cover checks), so thin walls, corners and overlapping prisms can be misjudged; cover points may not actually be hidden and 'visible' enemies may not be.",
  "Cover search only considers points reachable in a straight walkable line within 75 m and only the three nearest current threat positions; it cannot plan a route around a building to the far side, and A* has uniform cost with no exposure or threat term.",
  "'Many threats' is true whenever any unseen attacker hits it, so a single hidden shooter forces cover mode; 'outranged' only considers lasers.",
  "Fight mode uses no pathing (only 16-direction local steering toward a point 20 m away), and roof/air states disable pathing; no deliberate roof play, high ground or jump evasion.",
  "Navigation body radius is fixed at the base size although mechs grow 5% per cube; zone timing uses straight-line distance and a hard-coded walk speed, which can be late around large buildings.",
